mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%) signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current FEDFUNDS at 2.4% is below 2.5% threshold
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.5%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a recession and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 4.0%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current HOUST at 1230.0 and RSAFS at 504440.0 (both below prior levels)
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 250), the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 250, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of employment (PAYEMS > 150,000) signals a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 150,000, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 105 indicates a contraction in the manufacturing and industrial sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 105, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS < 150,000) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 3.8%) signals a deteriorating labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current PAYEMS at 150606.0 > 150000 and UNRATE at 3.8% (not above)
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS < 150000 AND UNRATE > 3.8, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing boom (HOUST > 1250), strong housing activity supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1250, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
